a: ID or ARN of the Outpost on which to run the capacity task. Both forms are accepted; the provider normalizes the value internally. Changing this value forces a new resource.

ID of a specific Outposts asset (hardware server) to target for the capacity task. If omitted, AWS selects an appropriate asset automatically. Discover valid asset IDs with the `aws_outposts_assets` data source.
ID of the Amazon Web Services Outposts order associated with the capacity task. Changing this value forces a new resource.
Region where this resource will be [managed](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#regional-endpoints).
Action to take if running instances block the capacity task. Valid values are `WAIT_FOR_EVACUATION` and `FAIL_TASK`. Changing this value forces a new resource.
Number of instances of `instance_type` that should be present after the task completes. Must be at least `1`. Changing this value forces a new resource.
Instance type for this pool entry. Must be an instance type supported by the target Outpost. Changing this value forces a new resource.
Set of EC2 instance IDs (of user-owned instances running on the Outpost) that the capacity task must not stop. At least one instance ID is required.

A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
